BILL NUMBER:  S1591

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the state finance law, in relation to establishing a
mentor-protege program for small and minority and women-owned business
concerns


 PURPOSE :
To establish mentor-protege programs in certain state agencies,
departments and authorities to develop the capabilities of small,
minority and women-owned business concerns.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Would require every state agency, department and authority which has
let. more than $10 million in service and construction contracts in
the prior fiscal year to institute a mentor-protege program. The Chief
Executive Officer of each agency, in consultation with the Department
of Economic Development's Division of Minority and Women's Business
Development and Division for Small Business, would establish
requirements for approval of contractors acting as mentor firms,
requirements for protege firms, and requirements for a process for
establishing mentor-protege agreements.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Mentor-protege programs create partnerships between established,
experienced state contractors and emerging small, minority or
women-owned businesses. Two public authorities, the New York City
School Construction Authority and the Port Authority of New York and
New Jersey, have established mentor-protege programs which have been
highly successful in enhancing the capabilities of small and minority
and women-owned business concerns and creating sources of reliable
contractors and subcontractors for public projects. The federal
government has had an active mentor-protege program since 1991, and
numerous states including Ohio, Texas, Delaware and Minnesota have
programs as well. The bill would extend this successful and proven
program to all large New York state agencies and public authorities.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2005-06: A.9068; Passed Assembly 145-0, Referred to Senate Finance.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None of specific note.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

summary: Requires state agencies, departments or authorities which let more than ten million dollars in service and construction contracts to establish mentor-protege programs to enable the development and success of small, minority, and women-owned businesses.
